newsitem.title: USA: U.S. would consider new N. Korea food aid appeal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. would consider new N. Korea food aid appeal.

text.p: The United States said on Monday it would consider seriously any new U.N. food appeal for North Korea and urged other countries to also contribute because the Stalinist state is facing a famine.

Washington has not been asked for any additional food aid by the U.N. World Food Program beyond $25 million recently donated but if another appeal is made "we would look at it very very seriously," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters.

Asked about reports that Japan and South Korea, among other countries, have not responded to a World Food Programme appeal several weeks ago for $95.5 million in food aid, Burns said: "We do hope that other countries will respond favourably ... we think that one ought to separate politicas from humanitarian need."

The World Food Programme on Monday called for large scale emergency aid to North Korea to prevent a famine that the U.N. agency said could turn into "one of the biggest humanitarian disasters of our lifetime."
Burns said the United States agreed that "there is a famine in North Korea."

The United States and South Korea met North Korea in New York nearly two weeks ago to hear Pyongyang's response to a U.S.-South Korea proposals for peace talks. North Korean negotiators said Pyongyang was willing to enter into the peace talks but conditioned its participation on more food aid, lifting U.S. trade sanctions and diplomatic recognition.
